content.comment_body: I recently acquired an ABB IRB140-6-81 robot arm with its control system. An ABB representative mentioned that robot IO can only be provided via an Ethernet connection to a PLC. Has anyone had experience with this setup? Appreciate any insights.

From my experience, ABB robot controllers can be expanded with additional physical IO cards. There may also be options for expansion using fieldbus cards like CAN, Profibus, or Profinet, though I'm not certain about every supported protocol. For accurate information, it's best to consult an ABB specialist directly, not just anyone involved at the site. Regards, [user_name]
Based on what I know, this isn't feasible. The [product_name] controller only supports Ethernet TCP/IP with the S7 protocol or Modbus TCP/IP, but does not handle Profinet I/O.

Knowing your purpose for connecting the [product_name] controller to the ABB robot would help. Is it just for expanding I/O? If you have the ABB manual, check for options to expand I/O with physical cards or fieldbus solutions. Select a controller based on the supported fieldbus protocols. In general, I believe the [product_name] controller won't communicate directly with an ABB controller. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are uncertain about the ability of the [product_name] controller to communicate with ABB robot controllers using Ethernet, particularly for I/O expansion. There is confusion over the supported protocols, such as Profinet I/O, which are necessary for ABB integration. Comments suggest that while [product_name] handles Ethernet TCP/IP with S7 or Modbus TCP/IP, it lacks compatibility with Profinet I/O, limiting possible integration. Community members advise checking ABB manuals and consulting with ABB specialists for further clarification.
analysis.user_expectations: User hopes to enable communication between a [product_name] controller and an ABB robot controller via Ethernet for I/O control. They seek confirmation of whether this integration is possible and want advice about compatible protocols and practical solutions.
